assumptions_made.assumption: Marcus Webb's request for a card that never declines is encoded as a $50,000 per month ceiling. Ramp requires every limit to carry an amount, so an unlimited card cannot be created.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [01:38], offering a practical equivalent to an unlimited card for CEO Marcus Webb: "Fifty grand a month?"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Marcus Webb's spend exceeds $50,000 in a calendar month the card declines — the outcome Priya Shetty warned would define the project. Confirm the ceiling with Marcus Webb before go-live.

assumptions_made.assumption: Marcus Webb is assigned the Business Admin role (full administrative access across the account). Ramp has an Owner role, but it is not among the roles this configuration can express, and Ramp does not permit inviting a user as Owner.
assumptions_made.source: department_roster.csv, row 2 — the roster records the job title CEO: "Marcus Webb,marcus@acme.example,CEO,G&A,,2019-02-01,NO LIMIT"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Marcus Webb receives full administrative rights over the Ramp account, which is broader than a spend-only role. If Acme Corp wants Marcus Webb to spend without administering the account, change the role to Business User before go-live.

assumptions_made.assumption: Kevin O'Rourke is assigned the Guest User role, the most restricted role available, matching the request for maximum lockdown for an external contractor.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Priya Shetty (Controller, Acme Corp), [04:52], describing the access required for contractor Kevin O'Rourke: "he should absolutely not see anything about anyone else's spend"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If the Guest User role is more restrictive than the work requires, Kevin O'Rourke cannot spend on job boards and recruiting stalls. Guest accounts also carry an automatic deactivation date — see the unsupported requests section.

assumptions_made.assumption: Priya Shetty is assigned the Business Admin role rather than Bookkeeper. Bookkeeper matches month-end close more precisely but cannot administer users or limits, and Priya Shetty was named as an administrator.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [05:41], naming who should be able to administer the Ramp instance, change limits and add users: "Priya and me. And probably Sana in IT for the user-management side"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Priya Shetty gains the ability to change limits and add users. If Acme Corp wants month-end close without administrative rights, change the role to Bookkeeper — but then a second administrator is needed, because Diane Marsh would be the only one.

assumptions_made.assumption: Sana Qureshi is assigned the IT Admin role, which grants people administration without any access to spend controls — the exact split requested.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Priya Shetty (Controller, Acme Corp), [05:52], limiting the scope of Sana Qureshi's administrative access: "Sana should not be able to change spend limits though. Just people stuff."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Acme Corp later wants Sana Qureshi to issue cards as well as manage people, the IT Admin role blocks it unless manager permissions are enabled for Sana Qureshi's direct reports.

assumptions_made.assumption: The $75 receipt threshold is an in-application policy setting and is deliberately left out of this configuration, because there is nowhere in the configuration to record it.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Priya Shetty (Controller, Acme Corp), [07:03], stating the receipt threshold: "Required over seventy-five dollars."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: No effect on card behaviour. If the deployment owner does not set the threshold in the Ramp application during setup, receipts are not required at all and month-end coding becomes manual.

assumptions_made.assumption: The $500 memo threshold is an in-application policy setting and is deliberately left out of this configuration, for the same reason as the receipt threshold.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Priya Shetty (Controller, Acme Corp), [07:03], stating the memo threshold: "And memo required for anything over five hundred."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: No effect on card behaviour. Without the setting, memos are not required and transactions arrive at month end without justification attached.

assumptions_made.assumption: The roster department values 'sales' and 'Sales' refer to one department, recorded as 'Sales'.
assumptions_made.source: department_roster.csv, row 23 — one of two roster rows using the lower-case spelling of the Sales department: "Fatima Diallo,fdiallo@acme.example,Account Executive,sales,ohaddad@acme.example,2022-06-06,2000"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If the two spellings are genuinely different departments, Fatima Diallo and Ivy Chen are placed in the wrong one and receive the wrong card programme.

assumptions_made.assumption: IT is recorded as a fifth department. The discovery call named four departments; the roster contains a fifth, and the roster was stated to take precedence.
assumptions_made.source: department_roster.csv, row 8 — the only roster row naming an IT department, which the discovery call did not mention: "Sana Qureshi,squreshi@acme.example,IT Administrator,IT,dmarsh@acme.example,2021-09-13,2000"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If IT should sit inside G&A, Sana Qureshi occupies a department of one and any future department-wide programme misses Sana Qureshi entirely.

assumptions_made.assumption: Han Zhao's monthly limit is recorded as $1,200, taken from the later of two roster rows carrying the same email address.
assumptions_made.source: department_roster.csv, row 33 — the second of two roster rows for the same email address, disagreeing with the first on the monthly limit: "Han Zhao,hzhao@acme.example,Staff Engineer,Engineering,vostrowski@acme.example,2020-07-06,1200"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Han Zhao receives $1,200 while every other engineer receives $500. Row order is a weak basis for the choice and this needs an answer from Acme Corp — see the conflicts section.

assumptions_made.assumption: Engineering's request-based access to the travel programme is recorded here rather than in the configuration, because this configuration has no field for issuance rules. Ramp does support this.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [04:05], describing how Engineering staff obtain travel cards: "Nobody in Engineering by default; they can request."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If the deployment owner does not set the travel programme to be requestable by Engineering, engineering staff cannot obtain a travel card at all and will book on personal cards.

assumptions_made.assumption: Spend limits are recorded in the format this exercise requires. In the live Ramp API the same objects are created through the funds endpoint.
assumptions_made.source: candidate/schemas/ramp_config_schema.json, top-level 'limits' section — the submission format is fixed by the exercise and is not changed to match the live API naming
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: No effect on Acme Corp. Relevant only to whoever applies this configuration to the Ramp API.

assumptions_made.assumption: Renata Flores receives the roster's $3,000 monthly limit. The discovery call asked for a 'decent limit' without naming a figure, and the roster was stated to take precedence.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Priya Shetty (Controller, Acme Corp), [05:12], requesting a card for office manager Renata Flores without naming an amount: "She should have her own card with a decent limit"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If 'decent' meant more than $3,000, Renata Flores hits declines on routine office spend, which is Renata Flores's core responsibility.

assumptions_made.assumption: 'Software-ish' is mapped to the single Ramp spend category 'SaaS / Software'.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Priya Shetty (Controller, Acme Corp), [03:14], describing what the software card must refuse: "And it should decline anything that isn't software-ish."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Purchases Acme Corp considers software but Ramp categorises elsewhere — hardware-bundled tools, some marketplaces — decline on the software card.

assumptions_made.assumption: 'Actual travel categories' is mapped to four Ramp spend categories: Airlines, Lodging, Taxi and rideshare, and Restaurants.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [03:27], listing the categories the travel programme should permit: "restricted to actual travel categories — airlines, hotels, rideshare, restaurants while traveling"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: Ramp categories are unconditional, so 'while traveling' cannot be expressed — travel cards also work at restaurants near the office. Car rental was not named and is excluded, which would block a rental booking.

assumptions_made.assumption: The $2,000 travel limit is recorded as one limit covering a named group of 11 travellers, which becomes one card per traveller when applied.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [04:05], naming who counts as a traveller: "Everyone in Sales, plus Marcus, plus me, plus Tom Reyes in Marketing"
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Acme Corp intended one shared $2,000 budget rather than $2,000 for each traveller, total travel exposure is eleven times the intended figure.

assumptions_made.assumption: Acme Corp operates as a single existing US entity. The packet names no legal entity and does not discuss more than one.
assumptions_made.source: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [00:47], describing the whole organisational structure for spend, with no mention of multiple legal entities: "Four departments for spend purposes."
assumptions_made.impact_if_wrong: If Acme Corp has more than one legal entity, every user is attached to the wrong one and locations must be added to separate the entities.

conflicts.description: Marcus Webb's spending limit. The roster records the text 'NO LIMIT' where a number is expected; the discovery call offers $50,000 per month as a practical equivalent, and Priya Shetty asks for a very high ceiling rather than none.
conflicts.source_a: department_roster.csv, row 2 — the limit column contains text rather than a number: "Marcus Webb,marcus@acme.example,CEO,G&A,,2019-02-01,NO LIMIT"
conflicts.source_b: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [01:38], offering a workable figure in place of an unlimited card: "Fifty grand a month?"
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded $50,000 per month. The rule that the roster takes precedence does not settle this one: 'NO LIMIT' is not a value Ramp can store, so the figure from the call is the only option that can be applied. Raised as a blocking question for Marcus Webb.

conflicts.description: Han Zhao's monthly limit. The roster contradicts itself — the same email address appears on two rows carrying different limits.
conflicts.source_a: department_roster.csv, row 10 — the first of two rows for this email address: "Han Zhao,hzhao@acme.example,Staff Engineer,Engineering,vostrowski@acme.example,2020-07-06,500"
conflicts.source_b: department_roster.csv, row 33 — the second of two rows for the same email address: "Han Zhao,hzhao@acme.example,Staff Engineer,Engineering,vostrowski@acme.example,2020-07-06,1200"
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded $1,200, taken from the later row. The rule that the roster takes precedence cannot settle a roster that disagrees with itself, so this rests on row order alone, which is a weak basis. Raised as a blocking question.

conflicts.description: The number of departments. The discovery call names four departments for spend purposes; the roster contains five.
conflicts.source_a: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [00:47], listing the departments for spend: "Four departments for spend purposes."
conflicts.source_b: department_roster.csv, row 8 — the roster row introducing a fifth department not named on the call: "Sana Qureshi,squreshi@acme.example,IT Administrator,IT,dmarsh@acme.example,2021-09-13,2000"
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded all five, including IT, following the stated rule that the roster takes precedence where the roster and the call disagree.

conflicts.description: Whether reimbursements continue. Diane Marsh states the goal is to eliminate reimbursements, then asks in the same exchange to keep reimbursements available for exceptions.
conflicts.source_a: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [06:48], stating the direction of travel: "We want to basically kill reimbursements."
conflicts.source_b: discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [06:48], stating the exception to that direction: "Keep reimbursements on for edge cases"
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Reimbursements remain enabled company-wide and are disabled on the Software programme, where a card-only rule was explicit. Read as a stated direction with a stated exception rather than a true contradiction.

conflicts.description: Whether the roster's manager column can be relied on. Diane Marsh confirms that the roster's manager column is correct; Priya Shetty immediately qualifies that the two most recent Marketing hires may be out of date after a reorganisation.
conflicts.source_a: discovery_call_01.txt — Jordan Lee (Deployment Lead, Genera), [06:22], confirming the source for reporting lines: "managers are as listed in the roster's manager column?"
conflicts.source_b: discovery_call_01.txt — Priya Shetty (Controller, Acme Corp), [06:26], qualifying that confirmation: "The roster's manager column is right for everyone except possibly the two newest Marketing hires"
conflicts.provisional_resolution: Encoded the roster's manager column as written for every user, following the explicit instruction not to hold up the work and not to invent an answer. Aisha Bello and Grant Sokol are raised as a non-blocking question.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A three-tier approval chain: spend under $500 approved automatically, $500 to $5,000 approved by the direct manager, and anything above $5,000 approved by Diane Marsh personally with no delegation.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: The Ramp API has no endpoint for creating approval policies. The requested tiers are recorded in this configuration as desired state, but cannot be applied programmatically.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no approval-policy write endpoint; only /blank-canvas-approvals/* (acts on existing instances) and GET /spend-programs/{id}/workflow-nodes (read-only); zero approval OAuth scopes. support.ramp.com 'Set up your spend approval policies', checked 2026-08-30 — tiered approval chains ARE configurable in Ramp's in-app approvals workflow builder, so this is a UI-only capability rather than a missing one.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Tiered approval chains are a standard Ramp feature, but are built in the approvals workflow builder inside the Ramp application rather than through the API. The tier structure requested is recorded here as desired state, and the deployment owner recreates it in Ramp before go-live. Routing by amount and by user role is available on every plan; more elaborate conditions require Ramp Plus, so confirm the plan tier first.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Approval by Diane Marsh for any new software vendor, regardless of the amount, including a ten-dollar monthly tool.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: The rule depends on whether a vendor is new, not on the amount. Ramp approval rules are triggered by amount, so a rule that catches every new vendor also catches every existing one. The policy recorded here is set at a zero threshold and therefore routes all software spend to Diane Marsh, which is broader than requested.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no approval write surface; additionally 'new vendor' is not threshold-shaped and approval_policies[].tiers[] is keyed only on threshold_usd_cents.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp cannot route an approval on the basis that a supplier is new; approval rules are driven by amount and by user role. The closest available control is a dedicated spend program for first-time suppliers with a low approval threshold, set up by the deployment owner in the Ramp application, accepting that it will also stop ordinary purchases above that amount. This requirement is therefore recorded as a process control rather than an automated one.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A card with no spending ceiling for Marcus Webb.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Every Ramp spend limit must carry a period and an amount. A $50,000 monthly ceiling is recorded in place of no limit, with the figure raised for confirmation.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — ApiFundSpendingRestrictionsRequestBody requires both 'interval' and 'limit', and limit.amount is a required integer; there is no unlimited sentinel.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp requires every spend limit to carry both a period and an amount; there is no unlimited setting, in the API or in the Ramp application. A deliberately high ceiling stands in for 'no limit', and the exact figure is recorded for the deployment owner to approve, because a high ceiling and no ceiling are different promises to the person holding the card.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A single $2,000 monthly travel limit covering the eleven named travellers.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp limits belong to one person, so a limit covering a group becomes one limit per traveller. Whether Acme Corp intended $2,000 for each traveller or $2,000 shared between all eleven is not stated in the packet and changes total exposure elevenfold.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — POST /funds requires a single user_id, so a group limit becomes one fund per member; is_shareable with /funds/{id}/members is the nearest shared-pool primitive and has different semantics (one shared pot, not N).
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp attaches a spend limit to one person at a time, so a limit described for a team becomes either a separate limit of that size for each member or a single shared pot the whole team draws down. Those are materially different outcomes and the wording of a request rarely settles which is meant, so the deployment owner should confirm the intent for each team-level limit before setup.

unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Receipt rules are a company policy setting in the Ramp application and have no equivalent in this configuration format, so the threshold is recorded in the assumptions above rather than in the configuration.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — no receipt-policy configuration resource; /receipts covers receipt objects and ingestion, not thresholds. Receipt rules are an in-app setting.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Receipt requirements are a standard Ramp policy setting, configured in the Ramp application rather than through the API, so the rule is not carried in the setup produced here. The deployment owner sets the receipt threshold during account setup; the omission is recorded so that nothing is assumed to already be in place.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A memo required on transactions over $500.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Memo rules are a company policy setting in the Ramp application, with no equivalent in this configuration format.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — /memos exposes memo objects but no memo-policy or threshold configuration surface; the rule is an in-app setting.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Memo and justification requirements are configured in the Ramp application rather than through the API. The deployment owner sets the memo threshold during account setup; the rule is not carried in the setup produced here, and that omission is recorded rather than quietly dropped.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Kevin O'Rourke must not see anything about anyone else's spend.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp limits spend visibility to a person's own reporting line, and the Guest User role is the most restricted role available, so this requirement is largely met. Ramp offers no way to guarantee it field by field through the API.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: support.ramp.com 'User roles overview', checked 2026-08-30 — transaction visibility follows the reporting chain, not department labels, and manager permissions are scoped to the manager's own team; that chain is settable via direct_manager_id on POST /users/deferred. Finer scoping (Custom Roles, entity restriction) exists in-app on Ramp Plus but is not API-creatable — Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) shows GET /roles is read-only.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp scopes spend visibility to a manager's own reporting line, so setting each person's manager correctly delivers most of this requirement directly. Anything beyond that — visibility that does not follow reporting lines — requires a Custom Role, which is configured in the Ramp application and is available on Ramp Plus. Confirm the plan tier before relying on it.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A continuing contractor account for Kevin O'Rourke, who works on an ongoing fractional basis.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp automatically sets a deactivation date six months after invitation on Guest User accounts unless that date is explicitly cleared. Left unchanged, Kevin O'Rourke's card stops working part-way through the engagement without warning.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — GUEST_USER accounts receive an automatic scheduled_deactivation_date six months from invite unless explicitly nulled; the field is not settable for admins or owners.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: A Guest User account (limited, occasional-use access) is automatically scheduled to deactivate six months after invitation unless that date is cleared. Anyone needing access for longer than six months, such as a contractor on a multi-year engagement, should either hold a different role or have the deactivation date cleared at setup. Every Guest User assignment is called out for the deployment owner to confirm.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: A virtual software card held by IT, and physical cards for the Sales team and for travellers.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Virtual cards are created by Ramp as part of issuing a spend limit rather than requested directly. Physical cards require a shipping address for each cardholder, and the packet contains none.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — POST /cards/physical exists (requires shipping_address and user_id) but virtual cards are GET-only and are issued via funds rather than created directly.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Both card types are available: a virtual card is issued alongside a spend limit, while a physical card is ordered explicitly and needs a shipping address for each recipient. Shipping addresses are not present in the material provided, so the deployment owner supplies one per physical cardholder before those cards can be ordered.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Adjusting the Software and Travel programmes after go-live once real spend is visible.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp spend programmes cannot be edited through the API once created. Both programmes should be reviewed carefully before creation.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) — /spend-programs has GET and POST only and /spend-programs/{id} is GET-only; there is no PATCH or DELETE, so programs are immutable via the API.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: A spend program cannot be edited through the API once created; later changes are made in the Ramp application instead. That makes the review of program definitions before go-live the cheapest point to change anything, and the deployment owner should treat it as the moment to settle names, limits and restrictions.

unsupported_api_requests.requested_feature: Distinct permission levels for a CEO, a VP Finance, a Controller, an office manager, an IT administrator and an external contractor.
unsupported_api_requests.reason_unsupported: Ramp offers a fixed set of roles with no seniority or scoping dimension, so each of Acme Corp's job titles is matched to the closest available role. Every non-obvious match is listed individually in the assumptions above.
unsupported_api_requests.evidence: Ramp Developer API specification (snapshot dated 2026-08-30) plus support.ramp.com 'User roles overview', checked 2026-08-30 — Ramp exposes six assignable roles with fixed, documented permission sets and no seniority or scoping dimension, so mapping customer job titles onto Ramp roles is a per-person judgement call.
unsupported_api_requests.proposed_manual_workaround: Ramp offers a fixed set of six assignable roles with defined permissions and no seniority or scoping dimension, so each job title is matched to the closest role by judgement rather than by rule. Every non-obvious match is recorded with the job title, the role chosen, and what that role can see and do, for the deployment owner to confirm before invitations go out.
